text:
Dear Sir or Madam

I've attached my employment contract with Ahornweid Management Ltd so you can see who I work for and when I started there.

I need advice quickly. I'm a caretaker for their buildings in Lausanne and I've had a really bad few weeks. I had to do my civil defence service, which was called up for this winter, and that service overlapped with my notice period. My colleague Owen Lüthi covered my buildings while I was away, so nobody can say the work was left undone.

On top of that I got pneumonia. My doctor wrote me off sick for ten days and I have the certificate. That sick leave overlapped with my notice period as well. I didn't choose to get ill, I caught it like half of Lausanne did this winter.

The notice itself: on 7 February 2026 Clara Hofer, the manager, gave me a letter saying they were ending my employment. She said it was 'not working out' and that was all.

I know they will say I was still on trial, and that's true, I had only started on 19 January so I was still in my trial period when she gave me the letter. But I'd like to know whether my service and my illness change anything about that notice. My wage was CHF 2,090 a month and I have rent to pay at Gartenstrasse 68.

Can you tell me what I can do and whether the dates matter here?

Thank you,
Jack Meier

EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (extract)

Between
Ahornweid Management Ltd, Lausanne, represented by Ms Clara Hofer, Property Manager (the employer)
and
Mr Jack Meier, Gartenstrasse 68, Lausanne (the employee)

1. Position
The employee is engaged as a building caretaker for the residential properties managed by the employer in Lausanne.

2. Start of employment
The employment begins on 19 January 2026.

3. Working time and pay
The employee works part-time according to the weekly rota. The gross monthly wage is CHF 2,090, paid at the end of each month.

4. Duties
Cleaning of common areas, small repairs, waste collection, contact with tenants.

Lausanne, 12 January 2026

For the employer: Clara Hofer
Employee: Jack Meier
